rules.title: RSO Annual Allowable Rent Increase Percentage
rules.requirement: Landlords of units covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) may raise rent once a year by an annually-announced percentage; for the period July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 that allowable increase is 3%. Starting February 2, 2026, landlords can no longer tack on an additional percentage increase for utilities on top of the allowable increase.

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies only to rental units subject to the LA Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO); tenants/landlords can check coverage via the City's ZIMAS lookup tool. Non-RSO properties are subject to different, state-law-based allowable increases.

rules.interaction: Separate monthly per-unit RSO ($1.61) and Systematic Code Enforcement Program/SCEP ($2.83) surcharges may also be passed through to tenants with proper written notice; these are described as separate from, and in addition to, the rent amount and the annual percentage increase. A statewide notice rule (Cal. Civ. Code § 827) separately requires 30 days' written notice for increases under 10%.
rules.quoted_span:
Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), effective
July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026
is
3%
rules.conflict_note: Document does not cite the specific RSO section number; '§ 151.06' is inferred as the generally known rent-adjustment section of the ordinance and should be verified. Also, the stated 3% rate applies only to the July 2025-June 2026 period, which had already ended by the 2026-10-01 query date; the document does not give the rate for the following period.

rules.title: Advance Written Notice Required for Rent Increases Under 10%
rules.requirement: California state law requires landlords to give tenants at least 30 days' written advance notice before a rent increase that is less than 10%.
rules.interaction: Applies alongside local rent-increase caps such as the LA RSO's annual percentage limit; a larger increase (10% or more, where permitted) requires longer (90-day) notice under the same state statute, which is not detailed in this document.
rules.quoted_span: State law requires landlords to provide 30 days' written advance notice of rent increases of less than 10%.
